passages.text: Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers at Shechem and said to them and to all the clan of his mother, “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal.
He went to Shechem.
He went to his mother’s brothers.
He spoke to them.
He also spoke to all the family of his mother’s father.
He said to them, “Please speak to all the leaders of Shechem for me.”
He said, “Ask them this question.”
“Is it better for you if seventy men rule over you?”
“These seventy men are all the sons of Jerubbaal.”
“Or is it better if only one man rules over you?”
“Remember this.”
“I am your own flesh and blood.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ בֶּן־ יְרֻבַּ֙עַל֙ שְׁכֶ֔מָה אֶל־ אֲחֵ֖י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶל־ כָּל־ מִשְׁפַּ֛חַת בֵּית־ אֲבִ֥י אִמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃ דַּבְּרוּ־ נָ֞א בְּאָזְנֵ֨י כָל־ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶם֮ מַה־ טּ֣וֹב לָכֶם֒ הַמְשֹׁ֨ל בָּכֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ כֹּ֚ל בְּנֵ֣י יְרֻבַּ֔עַל אִם־ מְשֹׁ֥ל בָּכֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וּזְכַרְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־ עַצְמֵכֶם וּבְשַׂרְכֶ֖ם אָנִֽי׃

passages.text: And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal, also called Gideon.
His mother’s brothers spoke to the leaders of Shechem.
They spoke about Abimelech.
They told the leaders all the words Abimelech had said.
The leaders of Shechem listened to these words.
Their hearts turned toward Abimelech.
They chose to follow Abimelech.
They said, “He is our brother.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֲחֵֽי־ אִמּ֜וֹ עָלָ֗יו בְּאָזְנֵי֙ כָּל־ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤ט לִבָּם֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ אָחִ֥ינוּ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal.
The leaders of Shechem supported Abimelech.
They gave Abimelech seventy pieces of silver.
They took this silver from the temple of Baal-berith.
Abimelech used the silver to hire men.
These men were worthless and reckless.
The men followed Abimelech.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנוּ־ לוֹ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף מִבֵּ֖יתּ בַ֣עַל בְּרִ֑ית וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֨ר בָּהֶ֜ם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים רֵיקִים֙ וּפֹ֣חֲזִ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal.
Abimelech went to his father’s house in Ophrah.
He killed his seventy brothers there.
All these brothers were sons of Jerubbaal.
He killed them on one stone.
Jotham was the youngest son of Jerubbaal.
Jotham survived.
Jotham hid himself.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א בֵית־ אָבִיו֙ עָפְרָ֔תָה וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֞ג אֶת־ אֶחָ֧יו בְּנֵֽי־ יְרֻבַּ֛עַל שִׁבְּעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ עַל־ אֶ֣בֶן אֶחָ֑ת וַיִּוָּתֵ֞ר יוֹתָ֧ם בֶּן־ יְרֻבַּ֛עַל הַקָּטֹ֖ן כִּ֥י נֶחְבָּֽא׃ס

passages.text: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Shechem gathered together.
The people of Beth-millo also gathered with them.
They met beside the oak tree.
This oak stood by the pillar in Shechem.
They made Abimelech their king.
passages.original: וַיֵּאָ֨סְפ֜וּ כָּל־ בַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ לְמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־ אֵל֥וֹן מֻצָּ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out: “Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.
passages.sermon:
Jotham was the youngest son of Jerubbaal.
Jotham survived because he hid when his brothers were killed.
Someone told Jotham what happened in Shechem.
Jotham went to the top of Mount Gerizim.
Jotham stood on the mountain.
Jotham raised his voice.
Jotham called out to the leaders of Shechem.
Jotham said, “Listen to me, leaders of Shechem.
May God listen to you.”
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְיוֹתָ֗ם וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַר־ גְּרִזִ֔ים וַיִּשָּׂ֥א קוֹל֖וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֑א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וְיִשְׁמַ֥ע אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
passages.sermon:
The trees wanted a king.
The trees decided to choose a king for themselves.
The trees spoke to the olive tree.
The trees said, "Be our king."
passages.original: הָל֤וֹךְ הָֽלְכוּ֙ הָעֵצִ֔ים לִמְשֹׁ֥חַ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ לַזַּ֖יִת מְלוֹכָה עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
passages.sermon:
The olive tree answered the other trees.
The olive tree said, “I produce oil.
My oil brings honor to God.
My oil brings honor to people.
Should I stop giving my oil?
Should I leave my purpose?
Should I go and rule over the trees?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַזַּ֔יִת הֶחֳדַ֙לְתִּי֙ אֶת־ דִּשְׁנִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־ בִּ֛י יְכַבְּד֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל־ הָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’
passages.sermon:
The trees wanted a king.
The trees spoke to the fig tree.
The trees said, "Come and be our king."
The trees asked the fig tree to rule over them.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ הָעֵצִ֖ים לַתְּאֵנָ֑ה לְכִי־ אַ֖תְּ מָלְכִ֥י עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’
passages.sermon:
The fig tree spoke to the other trees.
The fig tree said, “I give sweetness.
I give good fruit.
Should I stop giving my sweetness?
Should I stop giving my good fruit?
Should I leave my purpose?
Should I go and rule over the other trees?”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַתְּאֵנָ֔ה הֶחֳדַ֙לְתִּי֙ אֶת־ מָתְקִ֔י וְאֶת־ תְּנוּבָתִ֖י הַטּוֹבָ֑ה וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל־ הָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’
passages.sermon:
The trees spoke to the grapevine.
The trees said, "Come and be king over us."
The grapevine is a plant that produces grapes.
The trees wanted the grapevine to rule them.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ הָעֵצִ֖ים לַגָּ֑פֶן לְכִי־ אַ֖תְּ מָלוֹכִי עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
passages.sermon:
The grapevine spoke to the trees.
The grapevine said, “I make wine.
My wine brings joy to God.
My wine brings joy to people.
Should I stop making my wine?
Should I leave my purpose?
Should I go and rule over the trees?”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַגֶּ֔פֶן הֶחֳדַ֙לְתִּי֙ אֶת־ תִּ֣ירוֹשִׁ֔י הַֽמְשַׂמֵּ֥חַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל־ הָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’
passages.sermon: All the trees spoke to the thornbush.\r\nThey said, "You go.\r\nYou be king over us."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ כָל־ הָעֵצִ֖ים אֶל־ הָאָטָ֑ד לֵ֥ךְ אַתָּ֖ה מְלָךְ־ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’
passages.sermon:
The thornbush spoke to the trees.
The thornbush said, "If you truly make me king over you, come and take shelter in my shade."
The thornbush continued, "But if you do not, fire will come out from the thornbush."
This fire will burn up the cedars of Lebanon."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הָאָטָד֮ אֶל־ הָעֵצִים֒ אִ֡ם בֶּאֱמֶ֣ת אַתֶּם֩ מֹשְׁחִ֨ים אֹתִ֤י לְמֶ֙לֶךְ֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בֹּ֖אוּ חֲס֣וּ בְצִלִּ֑י וְאִם־ אַ֕יִן תֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מִן־ הָ֣אָטָ֔ד וְתֹאכַ֖ל אֶת־ אַרְזֵ֥י הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves— for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian, but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother— if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.
passages.sermon:
Jotham spoke to the people of Shechem.
Jotham was the only surviving son of Jerubbaal.
Jerubbaal is also called Gideon.
Jotham said, “If you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, then you have done well.
If you have treated Jerubbaal and his family with goodness, then you have done right.
If you have given Jerubbaal what he deserves, then you have acted justly.
My father Jerubbaal fought for you.
He risked his life for you.
He saved you from the hand of Midian.
But today you have turned against my father’s house.
You killed his seventy sons on one stone.
You made Abimelech king over the leaders of Shechem.
Abimelech is the son of my father’s maidservant.
You made him king because he is your brother.
If you have acted faithfully and honestly with Jerubbaal and his family today, then rejoice in Abimelech.
Let Abimelech also rejoice in you.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם־ בֶּאֱמֶ֤ת וּבְתָמִים֙ עֲשִׂיתֶ֔ם וַתַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וְאִם־ טוֹבָ֤ה עֲשִׂיתֶם֙ עִם־ יְרֻבַּ֣עַל וְעִם־ בֵּית֔וֹ וְאִם־ כִּגְמ֥וּל יָדָ֖יו עֲשִׂ֥יתֶם לֽוֹ׃ אֲשֶׁר־ נִלְחַ֥ם אָבִ֖י עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ אֶת־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיַּ֥ד מִדְיָֽן׃ וְאַתֶּ֞ם קַמְתֶּ֨ם עַל־ בֵּ֤ית אָבִי֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וַתַּהַרְג֧וּ אֶת־ בָּנָ֛יו שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ עַל־ אֶ֣בֶן אֶחָ֑ת וַתַּמְלִ֜יכוּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ בֶּן־ אֲמָתוֹ֙ עַל־ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י אֲחִיכֶ֖ם הֽוּא׃ וְאִם־ בֶּאֱמֶ֨ת וּבְתָמִ֧ים עֲשִׂיתֶ֛ם עִם־ יְרֻבַּ֥עַל וְעִם־ בֵּית֖וֹ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׂמְחוּ֙ בַּאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂמַ֥ח גַּם־ ה֖וּא בָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king over Israel.
The leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo made him king.
If you have not acted faithfully and honestly,
May fire come out from Abimelech.
May this fire destroy the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo.
May fire also come out from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo.
May this fire destroy Abimelech.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אַ֕יִן תֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מֵאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְתֹאכַ֛ל אֶת־ בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶ֖ם וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֑וֹא וְתֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִבַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וּמִבֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וְתֹאכַ֖ל אֶת־ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech.
passages.sermon:
Jotham was the son of Jerubbaal.  
Jotham ran away.  
Jotham escaped to Beer.  
Jotham lived in Beer.  
Jotham feared his brother Abimelech.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣נָס יוֹתָ֔ם וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בְּאֵ֑רָה וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י אֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ אָחִֽיו׃פ

passages.text: After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years, God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully, in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Abimelech and on the leaders of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a ruler in Israel.
He ruled for three years.
God acted during this time.
God sent a spirit of animosity.
This spirit came between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem.
The leaders of Shechem turned against Abimelech.
They acted deceitfully toward him.
God did this for a reason.
Abimelech had killed the seventy sons of Jerubbaal.
The leaders of Shechem had helped Abimelech kill his brothers.
God wanted justice for this crime.
God wanted the blood of the seventy sons to be avenged.
God wanted Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem to be punished for their actions.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧שַׂר אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ ר֣וּחַ רָעָ֔ה בֵּ֣ין אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וּבֵ֖ין בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְגְּד֥וּ בַעֲלֵי־ שְׁכֶ֖ם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃ לָב֕וֹא חֲמַ֖ס שִׁבְעִ֣ים בְּנֵֽי־ יְרֻבָּ֑עַל וְדָמָ֗ם לָשׂ֞וּם עַל־ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ אֲחִיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרַ֣ג אוֹתָ֔ם וְעַל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ חִזְּק֥וּ אֶת־ יָדָ֖יו לַהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת־ אֶחָֽיו׃

passages.text: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Abimelech.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Shechem acted against Abimelech.
They set up an ambush on the tops of the hills.
They waited for people traveling on the road.
They robbed everyone who passed by them.
Someone told Abimelech about these actions.
passages.original: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לוֹ֩ בַעֲלֵ֨י שְׁכֶ֜ם מְאָרְבִ֗ים עַ֚ל רָאשֵׁ֣י הֶהָרִ֔ים וַיִּגְזְל֗וּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲבֹ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃פ

passages.text: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.
passages.sermon:
Gaal was the son of Ebed.
Gaal had brothers.
Gaal and his brothers came to Shechem.
They entered the city.
The leaders of Shechem saw Gaal.
The leaders of Shechem trusted Gaal.
The leaders of Shechem put their confidence in Gaal.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֞א גַּ֤עַל בֶּן־ עֶ֙בֶד֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בִּשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְטְחוּ־ ב֖וֹ בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.
passages.sermon:
The people of Shechem went out into the fields.
They gathered grapes from their vineyards.
They trod the grapes.
They held a festival.
They went into the house of their god.
They ate.
They drank.
They cursed Abimelech.
passages.original: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וַֽיִּבְצְר֤וּ אֶת־ כַּרְמֵיהֶם֙ וַֽיִּדְרְכ֔וּ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ הִלּוּלִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱ‍ֽלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?
passages.sermon:
Gaal was the son of Ebed.
Gaal spoke to the people of Shechem.
Gaal said, "Who is Abimelech?"
Gaal said, "Who is Shechem, that we should serve him?"
Abimelech is the son of Jerubbaal.
Zebul is Abimelech's officer.
You should serve the men of Hamor.
Hamor is the father of Shechem.
Why should we serve Abimelech?
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־ עֶ֗בֶד מִֽי־ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ וּמִֽי־ שְׁכֶם֙ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֔נּוּ הֲלֹ֥א בֶן־ יְרֻבַּ֖עַל וּזְבֻ֣ל פְּקִיד֑וֹ עִבְד֗וּ אֶת־ אַנְשֵׁ֤י חֲמוֹר֙ אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וּמַדּ֖וּעַ נַעַבְדֶ֥נּוּ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

passages.text: If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Gaal son of Ebed spoke.
He wanted power over the people of Shechem.
He said, “If I ruled these people, I would remove Abimelech.”
He challenged Abimelech directly.
He said, “Gather your army and come out.”
passages.original: וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן אֶת־ הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְאָסִ֖ירָה אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לַאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ רַבֶּ֥ה צְבָאֲךָ֖ וָצֵֽאָה׃

passages.text: When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger.
passages.sermon:
Zebul was the governor of the city.
Gaal was the son of Ebed.
Gaal spoke words in the city.
Zebul heard the words of Gaal.
Zebul became very angry.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע זְבֻל֙ שַׂר־ הָעִ֔יר אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֖י גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־ עָ֑בֶד וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So he covertly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.
passages.sermon:
Zebul was the governor of the city.
Zebul acted secretly.
Zebul sent messengers to Abimelech.
Zebul told Abimelech, “Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem.
They are stirring up the city against you.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל־ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בְּתָרְמָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה֩ גַ֨עַל בֶּן־ עֶ֤בֶד וְאֶחָיו֙ בָּאִ֣ים שְׁכֶ֔מָה וְהִנָּ֛ם צָרִ֥ים אֶת־ הָעִ֖יר עָלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.
passages.sermon:
Zebul was the governor of the city.
Zebul spoke to Abimelech.
Zebul gave instructions to Abimelech.
Zebul said, “Get up tonight.
You must rise with the people who are with you.
Go to the fields.
Hide there and wait in ambush.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם לַ֔יְלָה אַתָּ֖ה וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתָּ֑ךְ וֶאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”
passages.sermon:
In the morning, when the sun rises, you must get up.
You must go forward against the city.
Gaal and the people with him will come out to face you.
You must do to them whatever you are able to do.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ תַּשְׁכִּ֖ים וּפָשַׁטְתָּ֣ עַל־ הָעִ֑יר וְהִנֵּה־ ה֞וּא וְהָעָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּוֹ֙ יֹצְאִ֣ים אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֥א יָדֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech gathered all the people who were with him.
They set out at night.
They went to Shechem.
They hid and waited near Shechem.
They divided into four groups.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֖וֹ לָ֑יְלָה וַיֶּאֶרְב֣וּ עַל־ שְׁכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה רָאשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Now Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.
passages.sermon:
Gaal was the son of Ebed.
Gaal went out from the city.
Gaal stood at the entrance of the city gate.
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech had men with him.
Abimelech and his men were hiding in ambush.
Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.
This happened as Gaal stood at the city gate.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־ עֶ֔בֶד וַיַּעֲמֹ֕ד פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְהָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ מִן־ הַמַּאְרָֽב׃

passages.text: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!” But Zebul replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”
passages.sermon:
Gaal was a man in Shechem.
Gaal saw people coming.
Gaal spoke to Zebul.
Gaal said, “Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains.”
Zebul answered Gaal.
Zebul said, “You see the shadows of the mountains as if they are men.”
passages.original: וַיַּרְא־ גַּעַל֮ אֶת־ הָעָם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ זְבֻ֔ל הִנֵּה־ עָ֣ם יוֹרֵ֔ד מֵרָאשֵׁ֖י הֶהָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ זְבֻ֔ל אֵ֣ת צֵ֧ל הֶהָרִ֛ים אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה כָּאֲנָשִֽׁים׃ס

passages.text: Then Gaal spoke up again, “Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak.”
passages.sermon:
Gaal was a man in Shechem.
Gaal spoke again.
He said, “Look, people are coming down from the center of the land.”
He also said, “One group is coming by the way of the Diviners’ Oak.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֣וֹד גַּעַל֮ לְדַבֵּר֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־ עָם֙ יֽוֹרְדִ֔ים מֵעִ֖ם טַבּ֣וּר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹאשׁ־ אֶחָ֣ד בָּ֔א מִדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֵל֥וֹן מְעוֹנְנִֽים׃

passages.text: “Where is your gloating now?” Zebul replied. “You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people you ridiculed? Go out now and fight them!”
passages.sermon:
Zebul spoke to Gaal.
Zebul was a leader in Shechem.
Gaal had spoken proudly against Abimelech.
Zebul said, “Where is your boasting now?”
Zebul reminded Gaal, “You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’”
Zebul pointed to the people coming.
Zebul said, “These are the people you mocked.”
Zebul told Gaal, “Go out now and fight them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו זְבֻ֗ל אַיֵּ֨ה אֵפ֥וֹא פִ֙יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר מִ֥י אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ הֲלֹ֨א זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָאַ֣סְתָּה בּ֔וֹ צֵא־ נָ֥א עַתָּ֖ה וְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem and fought against Abimelech, but Abimelech pursued him, and Gaal fled before him. And many Shechemites fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.
passages.sermon:
Gaal was a man in Shechem.
The leaders of Shechem supported Gaal.
Gaal went out in front of the leaders of Shechem.
Gaal fought against Abimelech.
Abimelech was a ruler and a warrior.
Abimelech pursued Gaal.
Gaal ran away from Abimelech.
Many people from Shechem fell wounded.
They fell all the way to the entrance of the city gate.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣צֵא גַ֔עַל לִפְנֵ֖י בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃ וַיִּרְדְּפֵ֣הוּ אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖נָס מִפָּנָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּל֛וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים עַד־ פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר׃

passages.text: Abimelech stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech stayed in the city of Arumah.
Zebul was an official in Shechem.
Zebul forced Gaal and Gaal’s brothers to leave Shechem.
Gaal and his brothers could no longer live in Shechem.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בָּארוּמָ֑ה וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ זְבֻ֛ל אֶת־ גַּ֥עַל וְאֶת־ אֶחָ֖יו מִשֶּׁ֥בֶת בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and this was reported to Abimelech.
passages.sermon:
The people of Shechem lived in the city of Shechem.
The next day came.
The people of Shechem went out into the fields.
Someone told Abimelech about this.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So he took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up against them and attacked them.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
He took his men with him.
He divided his men into three groups.
He hid with his men in the fields.
He watched the city.
He saw people coming out of the city.
He stood up against those people.
He attacked them.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָעָ֗ם וַֽיֶּחֱצֵם֙ לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֔ים וַיֶּאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִן־ הָעִ֔יר וַיָּ֥קָם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיַּכֵּֽם׃

passages.text: Then Abimelech and the companies with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate. The other two companies rushed against all who were in the fields and struck them down.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
He had companies of men with him.
Abimelech and his men rushed forward.
They took their stand at the entrance of the city gate.
Two other companies were with Abimelech.
These two companies rushed against everyone in the fields.
They struck down all who were in the fields.
passages.original: וַאֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וְהָרָאשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ פָּשְׁט֕וּ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וּשְׁנֵ֣י הָֽרָאשִׁ֗ים פָּֽשְׁט֛וּ עַֽל־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה וַיַּכּֽוּם׃

passages.text: And all that day Abimelech fought against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech fought against the city all that day.
He did not stop fighting until he captured the city.
He killed all the people who were in the city.
He destroyed the city.
He scattered salt over the city.
passages.original: וַאֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ נִלְחָ֣ם בָּעִ֗יר כֹּ֚ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיִּלְכֹּד֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת־ הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֖הּ הָרָ֑ג וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְרָעֶ֖הָ מֶֽלַח׃פ

passages.text: On hearing of this, all the leaders in the tower of Shechem entered the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Shechem heard what happened.
These leaders were in the tower of Shechem.
They went into the inner chamber.
This chamber was in the temple of El-berith.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּֽל־ בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־ שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־ צְרִ֔יחַ בֵּ֖ית אֵ֥ל בְּרִֽית׃

passages.text: And when Abimelech was told that all the leaders in the tower of Shechem were gathered there, he and all his men went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took his axe in his hand and cut a branch from the trees, which he lifted to his shoulder, saying to his men, “Hurry and do what you have seen me do.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Someone told Abimelech that all the leaders of the tower of Shechem had gathered together.
Abimelech took all his men with him.
They went up to Mount Zalmon.
Abimelech took an axe in his hand.
He cut a branch from the trees.
He lifted the branch onto his shoulder.
Abimelech spoke to the men who were with him.
He said, “What you have seen me do, hurry and do the same.”
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י הִֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כָּֽל־ בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־ שְׁכֶֽם׃ וַיַּ֨עַל אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ הַר־ צַלְמ֗וֹן הוּא֮ וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת־ הַקַּרְדֻּמּ֜וֹת בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּכְרֹת֙ שׂוֹכַ֣ת עֵצִ֔ים וַיִּ֨שָּׂאֶ֔הָ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־ שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֗וֹ מָ֤ה רְאִיתֶם֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מַהֲר֖וּ עֲשׂ֥וּ כָמֽוֹנִי׃

passages.text: So each man also cut his own branch and followed Abimelech. Then they piled the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them, killing everyone in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a violent leader.
He led his men in battle against the people of Shechem.
Each man with Abimelech cut a branch from the trees.
Each man carried his branch.
All the men followed Abimelech.
They brought the branches to the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.
They piled the branches against the inner chamber.
They set the branches on fire above the people inside.
The fire burned the inner chamber.
All the people in the tower of Shechem died.
About a thousand men and women died in the fire.
passages.original: וַיִּכְרְת֨וּ גַם־ כָּל־ הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ שׂוֹכֹ֗ה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֤י אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ עַֽל־ הַצְּרִ֔יחַ וַיַּצִּ֧יתוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם אֶֽת־ הַצְּרִ֖יחַ בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַיָּמֻ֜תוּ גַּ֣ם כָּל־ אַנְשֵׁ֧י מִֽגְדַּל־ שְׁכֶ֛ם כְּאֶ֖לֶף אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשָּֽׁה׃פ

passages.text: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against it, and captured it.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech went to the city of Thebez.
He set up camp at Thebez.
Abimelech captured the city.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ תֵּבֵ֑ץ וַיִּ֥חַן בְּתֵבֵ֖ץ וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men, women, and leaders of the city fled there. They locked themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.
passages.sermon:
There was a strong tower inside the city.
All the men in the city ran to the tower.
All the women in the city ran to the tower.
All the leaders of the city ran to the tower.
They locked themselves inside the tower.
They went up to the roof of the tower.
passages.original: וּמִגְדַּל־ עֹז֮ הָיָ֣ה בְתוֹךְ־ הָעִיר֒ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ שָׁ֜מָּה כָּל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֗ים וְכֹל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר וַֽיִּסְגְּר֖וּ בַּעֲדָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ עַל־ גַּ֥ג הַמִּגְדָּֽל׃

passages.text: When Abimelech came to attack the tower, he approached its entrance to set it on fire.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a leader and a warrior.
Abimelech came to the tower in the city of Thebez.
He fought against the people inside the tower.
He went up to the entrance of the tower.
He wanted to set the tower on fire.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ עַד־ הַמִּגְדָּ֔ל וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֛שׁ עַד־ פֶּ֥תַח הַמִּגְדָּ֖ל לְשָׂרְפ֥וֹ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, crushing his skull.
passages.sermon:
A woman stood on the roof of the tower.
Abimelech was at the entrance below.
The woman took an upper millstone.
She dropped the millstone down.
The millstone struck Abimelech on the head.
The stone crushed his skull.
passages.original: וַתַּשְׁלֵ֞ךְ אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחַ֛ת פֶּ֥לַח רֶ֖כֶב עַל־ רֹ֣אשׁ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַתָּ֖רִץ אֶת־ גֻּלְגָּלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He quickly called his armor-bearer, saying, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” So Abimelech’s armor-bearer ran his sword through him, and he died.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a violent leader who killed his seventy brothers.
A woman dropped a millstone on Abimelech’s head.
The stone crushed his skull.
Abimelech acted quickly.
He called to his armor-bearer.
He said, “Draw your sword and kill me.”
He did not want people to say, “A woman killed him.”
The armor-bearer obeyed Abimelech.
He ran his sword through Abimelech.
Abimelech died.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א מְהֵרָ֜ה אֶל־ הַנַּ֣עַר׀ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤ף חַרְבְּךָ֙ וּמ֣וֹתְתֵ֔נִי פֶּן־ יֹ֥אמְרוּ לִ֖י אִשָּׁ֣ה הֲרָגָ֑תְהוּ וַיִּדְקְרֵ֥הוּ נַעֲר֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃

passages.text: And when the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went home.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a ruler in Israel.
A woman killed Abimelech by dropping a millstone on his head.
The Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead.
Each Israelite returned to his own home.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father in murdering his seventy brothers.
passages.sermon:
God acted.
God repaid Abimelech for his wickedness.
Abimelech had murdered his seventy brothers.
Abimelech had done this evil to his father.
God brought this punishment on Abimelech.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֖ת רָעַ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ לְאָבִ֔יו לַהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־ שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶחָֽיו׃

passages.text: And God also brought all the wickedness of the men of Shechem back upon their own heads. So the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
passages.sermon:
God saw the men of Shechem do wicked things.
God punished the men of Shechem for their wickedness.
God made their evil come back on their own heads.
Jotham was the son of Jerubbaal.
Jotham spoke a curse against the men of Shechem.
God made Jotham’s curse come true for them.
passages.original: וְאֵ֗ת כָּל־ רָעַת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם הֵשִׁ֥יב אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּרֹאשָׁ֑ם וַתָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קִֽלֲלַ֖ת יוֹתָ֥ם בֶּן־ יְרֻבָּֽעַל׃פ
